title: TokenFlow Lab: an LLM streaming simulator
excerpt: A browser tool I built to see what different token rates look like in a chat response.
imageAlt: A green typewriter with blank paper curling across a wooden desk.
preview: TokenFlow Lab streams text you provide at a chosen token rate. You can change the speed while it runs, compare tokenizers, and switch between even timing and small bursts. It simulates the output phase; it doesn't measure model performance or time to first token.
takeaways: The TPS slider changes the stream as it runs.
The selected tokenizer determines the token count and boundaries.
Steady and realistic modes use different timing at the same target rate.

title: How prefix caching works (and how I broke it)
excerpt: I put a timestamp ahead of a 6,000-token shared prompt and lost the cache hits. Moving it fixed the problem.
imageAlt: Two paper strips with the same green ink impressions beside a printing roller.
preview: Prefix caching reuses KV state when requests start with the same tokens. I go through how vLLM, SGLang, OpenAI, and Anthropic handle it, then explain how a timestamp in my prompt builder stopped nearly 6,000 shared tokens from being reused.
takeaways: A shared prefix needs identical tokens, including formatting.
Each serving system has its own cache controls and reuse rules.
Putting timestamps after the shared context restored my cache hits.
